meta.name: Racines
meta.description: Two-week repeating rota template. Days are a ring: week 2 Dimanche is adjacent to week 1 Lundi.

coverage._overridesNote: Services that need more or fewer than requiredPerService. An override names a day and a slot, so it applies in every week of the cycle -- how busy a service is belongs to the day of the week, not to which half of the fortnight it is. Example: { "day": "Samedi", "slot": "Dinner", "required": 4 }.

solver._maxCostDropNote: A cost budget, not a shift count: how far above the cheapest shift-count distribution the search keeps looking before giving up. Compare against the weights below -- one uncovered shift is 1000, one temporary shift is 300.

officeLunch.note: One lunch per week set aside for admin in the office. She still counts towards the three and can step onto the floor if that service is short; the engine reports (S6) whenever she is load-bearing rather than genuinely free to do admin.

staff.name: Barbara
staff._repeatNote: Her two weeks are genuinely different jobs -- five lunches, no dinners, no weekend in week 1; nine shifts with doubles and weekends in week 2 -- so the pair repeats as a fortnight.

staff.name: Federica
staff._repeatNote: Cover, so nothing repeats: her two week specs are identical and each week is placed wherever the gap happens to be. Do not set this to 'weekly' -- it would force her to work the same shifts in both weeks, and since the shortfall is in week 1 only, she could not take it without also working week 2, where there is no room. That leaves week 1 understaffed.
staff._note: Leaving. Available to plug gaps but must not be relied on: target is 0 shifts with a ceiling of 6 per week, and every shift she takes is charged (weights.temporaryShift) so the engine uses her only where the permanent team cannot cover. Everything she covers is listed under TEMP/LEAVER EXPOSURE in the report -- those are the shifts that become gaps when she goes.

staff.name: Beatrice
staff._daysOffNote: Owed two in a row; would like 3.5. The preference is scored (S8) and reported when it is missed, but never fails a schedule and never costs anyone a shift -- put a wish in consecutiveDaysOff and the solver starts rejecting legal rotas.

rules._enforcePersonCycleRepeatNote: Each solved person carries a 'repeat': 'weekly' = the same rota every week (Veronica, Beatrice); 'cycle' = the contract itself differs between weeks and repeats over cycleWeeks of them (Barbara); 'none' = nothing repeats and each week is placed on its own, which is what cover staff need (Federica). Set enforcePersonCycleRepeat false to let a 'weekly' person's weeks differ after all.
rules._officeLunchCountsOnFloorNote: Suyeon is in the office for that lunch but can step onto the floor, so she counts towards the three and no fourth person is needed. Set false if that lunch must be fully covered by three others.
rules._daysOffScopeNote: 'week' = the required run of days off must be available in EVERY week; a run straddling the week boundary counts for both weeks it touches. 'cycle' = one qualifying run anywhere in the fortnight, which lets a person work a full 7-day week.
